assigned.title: A property suite gets a timeout of its own, not vitest's default
assigned.acceptance: packages/contracts declares its own vitest testTimeout, with the reason for the value written down, so its fast-check property suite is not running against a default it can exhaust under load. THIS CLOSES AN OPEN ITEM RATHER THAN OPENING ONE. Round 52 recorded a single observed-but-unreproduced failure in stream-candidate.property.test.ts and the lead could not reproduce it across ten seeds; the PL-0710 part-A work reproduced it deterministically and it was never seed-dependent. It is CONCURRENCY-dependent: the box has 2 cores, turbo's default concurrency is 10, the new @liberty/net-policy package takes the graph from 18 test tasks to 20, and 'refuses a licence endpoint that is not https, whatever else it is' -- which runs in 1.73s standalone -- measured 5.4s and 7.4s under that graph against vitest's 5000ms default. Characterised rather than re-rolled: the same tree at --concurrency=4 passes, and the same tree filtered to 19 tasks at default concurrency passes. Required: the timeout is justified against the suite's measured standalone cost and the headroom a loaded machine needs, not picked round; the config explains that a property suite's cost is a function of run count and machine load rather than of the code under test, so a default sized for unit tests is the wrong instrument; and NOTHING ABOUT THE PROPERTY ITSELF IS WEAKENED -- not the run count, not the generators, not an assertion. Raising a timeout to hide a genuinely slow property would be the same mistake one level out, so if the suite is slow for a reason the code should answer for, say so instead. Out of scope: a turbo concurrency cap, which is a CLI flag rather than a turbo.json key and is a CI decision.
assigned.notes: Found 2026-09-20 during PL-0710 part A. The failing command is npx turbo run test --force at turbo's default concurrency, reproduced 2 of 2. packages/contracts has no vitest.config.ts at all today. packages/media-engine/vitest.config.ts is the house precedent for a package-local config that exists to keep a machine-dependent assertion out of the incidental run, and its header states the reasoning this task should follow.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force AT TURBO'S DEFAULT CONCURRENCY, exit 0, 20 of 20 tasks and 0 cached, 2565 passed 1 skipped. That is the command that matters, because it is the one that was failing. npx vitest run --root packages/contracts alone: 8 files, 202 passed. THE RED IS THE SUBAGENT'S, NOT MINE, AND THE RECORD SAYS SO. The agent that found this reproduced the failure two times out of two at default concurrency -- 'Test timed out in 5000ms' on 'refuses a licence endpoint that is not https, whatever else it is' -- and characterised it rather than re-rolling: 2 cores, turbo default concurrency 10, the new net-policy package taking the graph from 18 test tasks to 20, that test measured at 5.4s and 7.4s under the graph against a 1.76s standalone cost for the whole 31-test file. The same tree passed at --concurrency=4 and passed at default concurrency filtered to 19 tasks. I THEN RAN THE RED DIRECTION MYSELF AND IT DID NOT REPRODUCE: with this file removed, the same command on the same tree exited 0. So this is NOT a demonstrated red-to-green repair, and the config comment now says that in terms. It is headroom for a suite measured to be running at roughly a third of the budget it was held to, with no margin, which is a latent fragility whether or not it fires on a given afternoon. Round 52's single unexplained failure in this same suite is BEST EXPLAINED by this and is not thereby proven to be it; that item stays open rather than being closed on a hypothesis. Nothing about the property was weakened -- run count, generators and assertions are untouched, and the only file changed is a new packages/contracts/vitest.config.ts.

recommended.title: Contract module boundaries
recommended.acceptance: Shared vocabularies live in their own leaf modules, domain contracts live in one module each, index.ts is a re-export-only compatibility barrel rather than the authoritative public surface, and a wildcard exports map lets a new domain contract be added without touching package metadata or the barrel; no cycle-driven z.lazy remains and structural regressions prove the boundary rather than merely reflecting it; no schema behaviour changes

recommended.acceptance: GitHub becomes the shared state bridge for Claude Desktop and OpenAI review without manual file copying
